decisions.quote: To this end, our analyses built on previous work by Hille and Schupp (2015) aiming to replicate their findings. Contrary to the precursor study, our main results indicate a long-term association with cognitive skills, but not with academic achievement. Further, our analyses suggest that openness, conscientiousness, and perceived control are all positively associated with musical participation, thus corroborating and expanding previous findings (e.g., Corrigall et al., 2013).
decisions.reason: The abstract statement quoted in the shipped row affirms a broad positive association between musical training and non-musical skills rather than an overall replication verdict on Hille and Schupp (2015). When directly comparing their results to the precursor study, the authors explicitly contrast their cognitive skill and academic achievement findings while corroborating personality associations, which is mixed.
